title: Coming and going: ていく and てくる
summary: 来る always moves toward where the speaker is, 行く away from it. Attached to a て-form they describe change in space, in time and in how you feel.

blocks.text: **来る** can only mean moving from somewhere the speaker is **not** to the place where the speaker **is** (in mind as well). **行く** is looser: it moves away, or between two places the speaker is not at. That is why you cannot tell someone on the phone "I'll come to you" with 来る: you say 行く.
With a て-form, the helper keeps the same direction. 持って**くる** brings something toward me; 持って**いく** takes it away. Then the picture stretches to **time** and to **feeling**.

blocks.en: I'll take a lunch (away from here).
It has started to rain. (rain came toward the present)

blocks.jp: これからも日本語を勉強していく。
blocks.en: I will keep studying Japanese from now on. (moving forward in time)

blocks.text: **くる** is also a movement toward **my own state of mind**. 分かる means "be clear", so as you study, math *comes* to be clear to you. And **〜てきた** sounds like the change touches me or us, while **〜ていった** reports it from outside.

blocks.jp: だんだん数学が分かってくる。
blocks.en: Math gradually becomes clear to me.
It has been getting colder lately. (I feel it)

items: **来る**: toward the speaker's place, time or state. **行く**: away from it.
**〜てくる**: change arriving toward now; **〜ていく**: change continuing away, into the future.
**くる** can be subjective (it touches me); **いく** can be objective.
There are no strict rules: use the picture, and let immersion fill it in.

questions.instruction: On the phone, how do you say "I'm coming to your place now"?
options: 今からそちらに行きます
今からそちらに来ます
今からそちらにいます
今からそちらにくれます
questions.note: 来る cannot be used for going to where you are not.
持ってくる: bring toward here.

options: I will take a lunch with me
I will bring a lunch here

questions.note: Rain came toward the present moment.

questions.prompt: これから日本語をもっと勉強して＿＿。 (I will keep going from now on)
questions.note: Moving on into the future: いく.

questions.prompt: 最近、だんだん寒くなって＿＿。 (and I can feel it)
questions.note: きた: the change comes toward me and I feel it.

questions.prompt: 来る can be used for movement away from the speaker.
questions.note: 来る is always toward the speaker's place.

questions.instruction: Why is 分かってくる used for "come to understand"?
options: Math comes toward me in my mind
questions.note: くる covers movement toward my own state of mind.

questions.instruction: Which one feels like the change affects me or us?
Tap the word that points forward in time, away from now
Which one reports the cooling from outside, without involving me?
questions.note: 〜ていった is the outside-looking report.
